page.title: OpenAI’s mathematics release, read and checked
page.description: Every family of OpenAI’s mathematics release on one map, with a list beside it: what each family claims, what its Lean states, who has checked it, and where to read it.
page.redirect_text: The map of the release is now the front page.
page.independent: An independent reader of the release, not affiliated with OpenAI.
page.nojs: The map needs JavaScript. The list below names every family, with a link to each.

release.s1: OpenAI published {manuscripts_current} current papers in {families} families of related results, across {disciplines} disciplines.
release.s2: {statements_lean} Lean challenge files come with them, linked to {families_with_lean} of the families.
release.s3: OpenAI’s Lean catalogue names {statements_lean_main_results} of the {statements_lean} Lean challenge files as main results.
release.s4: Inside the release, {internal_citation_edges} ordered pairs of papers are joined by a citation, and the papers cite {external_works_cited} works outside it. OpenAI has withdrawn {manuscripts_withdrawn} papers and replaced {manuscripts_previous_editions} with later editions.
release.s5: The atlas credits public work under {community_people} names where it uses that work, and attaches {community_findings} findings to the results they concern.

key.heading: What the colours mean
key.intro: Each colour says what two outside readers find the release’s Lean states for a family’s headline result.
key.all: Both find the whole headline stated or implied
key.part: Part of it, or a narrower statement
key.other: A supporting or a different result
key.none: No Lean statement in the release
key.size: A disc’s area grows with the number of paper results and Lean statements it shows.
key.citations: Inside a discipline, pointing at a family draws its citations to the families beside it: brick where its papers cite, grey where they are cited.
key.readers: The readers are MathVet and Carlos Toledo’s cert-machine; each one’s own words are on every family page.

items.name: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture
items.why: Erdős conjectured that a set of positive integers whose reciprocals add up to infinity contains arithmetic progressions of every length. The family’s one paper claims a proof.

items.name: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
items.why: OpenAI’s catalogue describes a proof that no Dirichlet L-function, the Riemann zeta function included, has a zero with real part greater than 7/8.

items.name: The spacetime Penrose inequality
items.why: Penrose’s inequality bounds the mass of a spacetime from below by the smallest area enclosing its black holes. OpenAI’s catalogue describes a proof, under stated hypotheses, in every spatial dimension from three up.

items.name: Borsuk’s conjecture in dimension nine
items.why: Borsuk asked whether every bounded set in n dimensions splits into n + 1 pieces of smaller diameter. The paper constructs a set in dimension nine that does not.

bands.index_intro: The same release as the map, as a list. Each family opens its page.
bands.release_numbers: Every number, with how it was counted
bands.checked_intro: Each check is reported by the person or group named. The atlas shows their records beside the results they reach and has not repeated them.
bands.checked_cert: re-ran the release’s Lean files through Comparator with a second kernel, checked finite parts of some results by exact computation, and read each family’s Lean against its headline.
bands.checked_mathvet: re-ran the Lean files in a sandbox and read each family’s Lean against its headline under a published rubric.
bands.checked_neal: re-ran the Lean files with Lean’s kernel and recorded the time and memory each took.
bands.checked_hol: proved steps of some results again in HOL Light, with negative controls that must fail.
bands.checked_erdos: links families to the Erdős problems they address. A link is not a check.
bands.checked_more_link: Every source, with what each one reports
bands.help_intro: Each contribution covers one result or one page, and is credited by name on the pages it changes.
bands.help_without: Open a short form on GitHub to explain a result, check a Lean statement against its paper, or report a problem with one page.
bands.help_with: Give your assistant the start-here guide from the repository. It helps you choose one useful note, drafts it privately and leaves the signing to you.
bands.help_queue: Some Lean files have a specific reason to be read first.
